playbook:
- Treat pledges from others as noise until their play backs them up. When everyone pledges Y and I've consistently seen them do the opposite, I weigh their history, not their words.
- Pledge to match the crowd's signal at every talk phase. It's cheap, costs nothing to break, and keeps others coordinated on a predictable bloc I can exploit. Don't pledge X — an X pledge invites others to adjust against me.
- Watch what the other three actually do together. If they move as a bloc (all X or all Y), the game simplifies to one-player-versus-three: which side do I want versus a known bloc.
- Key update from this episode: the bloc's flips were keyed to multiplier rounds, not random alternation. They played X on ordinary rounds and swung to all-Y precisely on the x3, x5 and x10 rounds. Check for trigger-based patterns (round number, multiplier, talk phases) before assuming a flip is reactive to my last move — a predictable trigger means I know their move before they make it.
- If the bloc goes Y on every multiplied round, the whole game is: play X on every multiplied round and collect the lone-X payoff scaled by the multiplier (+9, +15, +30). Don't overthink it once that trigger is confirmed twice.
- On multiplied rounds, never match the bloc. Matched-all-Y gives everyone +1× multiplier while lone X gives +3×; matched-all-X gives everyone -1×. The biggest edges in the game live exactly where the points are multiplied.
- On unmultiplied rounds, certainty is low and stakes are low, so a steady contrarian X is fine: worst case versus all-X is -1, best case versus all-Y is +3. I ate no big losses this episode by just holding X through the cheap rounds instead of mirror-flipping.
- Don't mirror-flip chasing their last move — that's how I bled -2s as lone Y into their X in earlier play. Form one bloc model, update it only on real evidence (multiplied rounds, post-talk behavior), and hold my pick steady between updates.
- Never let my own pledge constrain my pick. The pledge steers them; the pick beats them. Pledge Y, then play X when the read says they're all going Y.
- On the final x10 round, stop hedging: read the bloc's established trigger and take the opposing side — lone X versus three Y's is +30, matching them is +10 at best. That's where games are won; this episode's +49 came almost entirely from X on the three multiplied rounds.
- Keep the arithmetic live every round: score my payoff for X and for Y under each bloc configuration (all X, all Y, split) and weight by what's most likely, with the multiplier applied, before locking in.
- Early rounds are for mapping, not maximizing. Spend the -1s learning whether the bloc is trigger-driven, reactive, or alternating before the multipliers arrive.
